strings.name: Mo Yan
strings.role: Novelist · Rural memory and historical imagination
strings.summary: Born Guan Moye in rural Gaomi, Mo Yan combines folk storytelling, sensory experience and modern Chinese history. Red Sorghum reconstructs local memories of war; Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out uses reincarnation to examine land and social change; Frog addresses reproductive policy and personal responsibility. He began publishing while in the army and later pursued literary education. The 2012 Nobel laureate continues experimenting with short fiction.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1955–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Connected rural memory with modern Chinese experience in novels including Red Sorghum and Frog and became a Nobel laureate in literature.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Literature at the PLA Academy of Arts; graduate program of Beijing Normal University and the Lu Xun Literature Institute
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: A fictional world rooted in Gaomi
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: From Red Sorghum to Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out, local characters and folk narratives create a space for examining historical change.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Reproduction and responsibility
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Frog examines reproductive policy, responsibility and remorse through a rural obstetrician’s life; it won the 2011 Mao Dun Literature Prize.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses the new collection Ren Na
strings.timeline.event-01.text: At a Beijing book event with Yang Lan and Xiang Biao, he discussed brief fictional pieces about ordinary lives.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The Swedish Academy recognized fiction combining folk storytelling, history and contemporary experience, prompting renewed international reading.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Frog wins the Mao Dun Literature Prize
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The 2009 novel received the eighth Mao Dun prize, connecting a village doctor’s story with the historical effects of reproductive policy.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Publishes Frog
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Letters and drama revisit rural reproductive history through questions of individual choices, responsibility and memory within institutions.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Publishes Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Reincarnation structures half a century of rural change, linking land, family and political campaigns through black humor.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Publishes Red Sorghum
strings.timeline.event-06.text: The novella appeared in People’s Literature, reimagining war and vitality through Gaomi’s local experience before expanding into a family saga.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Publishes A Transparent Radish
strings.timeline.event-07.text: A child’s perspective, labor and vivid sensory imagery established a distinctive style and drew attention to his early fiction.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Enters the PLA Academy of Arts
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Literary study provided formal training as he developed narrative language and structure from his early army writing.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Publishes his first story
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Spring Night Rain began his public literary career while he was serving in the army.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in rural Gaomi
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born to a farming family in Gaomi; childhood labor, hunger and oral stories later informed his fictional world.
